I am writing to formally complain about the treatment and behaviour I experienced at Priory Gardens GP Surgery in Dunstable.

On Friday 16th January 2026, I attended a pharmacy as I was concerned I may have a urinary tract infection (UTI). The pharmacy explained that they were unable to test my urine sample. After I described my symptoms, which included abdominal pain and feeling nauseous, I was advised that I could potentially have pyelonephritis and was strongly signposted to attend my GP surgery as a priority. I was also advised to contact 111, but told to attend my GP first. I was given documentation to take with me.

I attended Priory Gardens GP Surgery with this paperwork. At reception, the receptionist looked at my notes and then went to speak to her manager. The manager then came out and spoke to me in a very rude and unprofessional manner, raising her voice at me. I tried to explain that the pharmacy could not test my urine and that I had been advised to attend my GP urgently, but I was repeatedly told there were no appointments and that I must call 111.

I explained that every time I call 111, I am directed back to my GP surgery, meaning I am being passed back and forth without receiving any care. I tried to explain this calmly, but the manager dismissed me and continued to speak over me.

The manager then stated that I could not be seen due to my “medical history.” This was extremely upsetting, as she did not review my medical history in front of me, does not know me personally, and provided no explanation for this comment. I found this remark inappropriate and unprofessional.

I also explained that I had called at 8am and again at 1pm, and on both occasions was told there were no appointments available. Despite clearly being unwell and presenting with concerning symptoms, I was refused any form of assessment or support.

This experience is not isolated. During my pregnancy, I repeatedly contacted the surgery and struggled to be seen. I was only seen once, and later found out I had Group B Strep, yet no appropriate action or support was provided. This has left me with a complete lack of trust in the care provided by this surgery.

The behaviour of the reception manager was unacceptable. Shouting at a patient, being dismissive, and refusing to listen is not acceptable under any circumstances. This is not appropriate customer service or patient care.

Due to the repeated poor treatment and lack of support, I will be moving both myself and my daughter from this GP surgery. However, I feel it is important to formally raise this complaint so that this behaviour can be addressed and does not continue to happen to other patients.
